title: Revelation is immediate or mediate; immediate revelation is given to God's messengers by secret inspiration
pass_a_gloss: XI. And it is immediate or mediate. That is generally of the ambassadors, but this of those to whom they are sent. I say generally, because sometimes even to those who are not ambassadors it is granted for their own information, as to Joseph Matthew 1:20 and 2:13, more, in the same place verse 12. XII. Immediate, by which God disclosed his word to his ambassadors through secret inspiration, and placed it on their mouth to be announced to others.
pass_b_english: XI. Revelation is also immediate or mediate. Immediate revelation belongs generally to the ambassadors; mediate, to those to whom they are sent. I say "generally," because sometimes even those who are not ambassadors receive it for their own instruction — as Joseph did ([[Matthew 1:20 >> Bible:Matthew 1:20]]; [[Matthew 2:13 >> Bible:Matthew 2:13]]; still more, [[Matthew 2:12 >> Bible:Matthew 2:12]]).
XII. Immediate revelation is that by which God disclosed his word to his ambassadors through secret inspiration and set it on their mouth to be announced to others.
source_text:
XI. Estque immediata aut mediata. Illa fere legatorum est, haec vero eorum ad quos legantur. Fere dico, quia aliquando etiam iis, qui non sunt legati, conceditur sui ipsorum informationem, ut Josepho Mat. 1. 20. & 2. 13. magis, ibidem v. 12.

XII. Immediata, qua Deus legatis suis verbum suum per arcanam inspirationem patefecit, eorumque ori imposuit aliis renunciandum.
